lines.japanese: 心の広い人間でありたいとも思うんだ。
lines.english: I'd also like to be bighearted.

lines.japanese: ちょっとやそっとのことでは波風を立てない、妬まれても罵られても笑って許せる──そんな人間に私はなりたい。
lines.english: Someone who doesn't make waves over every little thing, who can smile and forgive people even when they envy her or insult her. That's the kind of person I want to be.

lines.japanese: なにも博愛とか反戦とか、そういう立派な大言を並べるつもりはない。もっと日常レベルで、単にヤなこと全部スルーできたら楽だろうなあって、それだけの話。
lines.english: I'm not planning to make grand pronouncements about universal love or opposition to war. I mean on a more everyday level. Wouldn't life be easier if I could just ignore everything unpleasant? That's all.

lines.japanese: だってさ、世の中には不条理なことが多いでしょう。
lines.english: Because there's a lot in this world that makes no sense, right?

lines.japanese: ことっていうか、人間？
lines.english: Or rather, a lot of people?

lines.japanese: 有り体に言っちゃうとさ、ワケワカランやつが多いでしょ。いや多いよ。多いって絶対。
lines.english: To put it plainly, aren't there a lot of people you just can't figure out? There are. There really are. Definitely.

lines.japanese: 気を付けなー？　あのね、ワケワカランやつがワケワカランことでワケワカランうちに恨んでたりするからねホント。もー、気が滅入るったらないよ。
lines.english: Watch out, okay? People you can't figure out can end up resenting you for reasons you can't figure out, before you've even figured out what's happening. Seriously. It's so depressing.

lines.japanese: たとえば彼と彼。
lines.english: Take him and him, for instance.

lines.japanese: 「ま、結局んとこはさ、映画が芸術たりえたのって商業主義に迎合するまでの話なんだよね。いかに大衆を惹きつける予告編が作れるかに拘泥しちゃってる時点で、あの分野はもう終わってるんだよ」
lines.english: “Well, in the end, film could only qualify as art until it started pandering to commercialism. Once the whole field became obsessed with making trailers that would attract the masses, it was already finished.”

lines.japanese: と力説する大衆Ａ。
lines.english: So declares Member of the Masses A.

lines.japanese: この、私の横に（断りもなく勝手に）並んで歩きながらびっくりするほど面白くない話を延々垂れながしているのが、去年同じクラスだったＡ君（仮名）。で──
lines.english: The one walking beside me (without asking, entirely of his own accord), pouring out an endless stream of astonishingly uninteresting talk, is A (not his real name), who was in my class last year. And—

lines.japanese: ──あっちの、いまこっちをフンとひと睨みして通りすぎていったのが、Ａ君の親友だったＢ君（仮名）。
lines.english: —the one who just gave us a contemptuous look as he passed is B (also not his real name), who used to be A's best friend.

lines.japanese: かつてふたりは、休み時間などに仲良くミュージシャンを批判したり野球監督を批判したり漫画雑誌を批判したり日本経済を批判したりしていた。
lines.english: The two of them once spent their breaks happily criticizing musicians, baseball managers, manga magazines, the Japanese economy, and so on.

lines.japanese: あるとき、いよいよ聞くに耐えかねた私が、うっかり「君ら何様だ」とライトなたしなめを入れてしまって──思えばこれが失敗だったんだろう。
lines.english: One day, when I finally couldn't stand listening anymore, I let a mild rebuke slip: ‘Who do you two think you are?’ In retrospect, that was probably my mistake.

lines.japanese: 私の発言した意図とは裏腹に、彼らは「うへえ、渡来こえー！」などとはしゃいでいた。
lines.english: Completely missing the point, they got all excited. ‘Whoa, Watarai's scary!’

lines.japanese: 次の日ふたりは私のツッコミを期待して、聞こえよがしなハイボリュームで森羅万象あらゆるものを批判しはじめた。
lines.english: The next day, hoping I'd make another sharp comment, they started criticizing absolutely everything at a volume calculated to make sure I heard.

lines.japanese: 偉ッそうに体育祭準備委員の不手際を糾弾しながら、しかし明らかにチラチラ、チラチラとこちらを窺っている視線に私はほとほと参ってしまい、またしてもつい「おまえの祭りか」とたしなめてしまった。
lines.english: They were pompously denouncing the sports festival committee's failings, but kept so obviously looking my way—glance, glance, glance—that I couldn't take it. Again, I couldn't help myself: ‘Is it your festival?’

lines.japanese: それがどうもフレンドリーな軽口と受けとられたらしく（まあ、たしかにそういうトーンで発声したんだけどもさ）、やはり彼らは「ひゃあ、明日香さまに怒られちったあ」などと浮かれていた。
lines.english: Apparently, they took that as friendly banter (well, yes, that was the tone I used), and once again got all excited. ‘Oh nooo, Princess Asuka scolded us!’

lines.japanese: うざっ。
lines.english: So annoying.

lines.japanese: それからだったと思う。それなりに一見さんへのバリアを張っているはずの私に、彼らが厚かましく近付いてくるようになったのは。
lines.english: I think that was when they started brazenly approaching me, despite the fairly substantial barrier I thought I kept up against newcomers.

lines.japanese: しかしその一方で、彼らふたりはみるみる険悪な仲になっていった。そして私が片方といるとき、もう片方は決まって嫌ぁな空気を漂わせるのである。
lines.english: Meanwhile, their relationship grew nastier by the day. Whenever I was with one of them, the other would invariably make the atmosphere unpleasant.

lines.japanese: 何故か？　知らないよ。言わせないでよ、察したくもない。
lines.english: Why? I don't know. Don't make me say it. I don't even want to guess.

lines.japanese: 「はあ……気が滅入る……」
lines.english: “Ugh... This is depressing...”

lines.japanese: 「でしょ！　ヤバいよね、最近のオスカーも」
lines.english: “Right? The Oscars have been terrible lately, too.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、なに？」
lines.english: “Huh? What?”

lines.japanese: 「心の広い人間になりたい」
lines.english: “I want to be bighearted.”

lines.japanese: 「はっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 心の広い人間になりたい。
lines.english: I want to be bighearted.

lines.japanese: 耳を疑うほど退屈な話でも心から楽しんで受けとめられる度量の大きさ。女の腐ったような恨みがましい視線さえ笑って赦せる寛大な精神。そういう海のような心を持ちたい。
lines.english: Generous enough to genuinely enjoy talk so boring I can hardly believe my ears. Magnanimous enough to smile and forgive even those spiteful, bitchy looks. I want a heart as vast as the sea.

lines.japanese: 面倒なしがらみを面倒とは感じない、俗世にいながらにして解脱した聖者のような人間になりたい。
lines.english: I want to be someone who doesn't find tiresome social obligations tiresome. An enlightened saint, free of worldly attachments while still living in the world.

lines.japanese: まあ、いつかね。理想としてね。現実的ではないけどね。
lines.english: Well, someday. As an ideal. It's not realistic, though.

lines.japanese: そのとき視界に入ったクラスの女子。んまあ、なんて良いところに！　いますぐ駆けよりハグせねば。
lines.english: Just then, I spot a girl from my class. Oh my, what perfect timing! I must rush over and hug her this instant.

lines.japanese: 「ごめ、友達いたから」
lines.english: “Sorry, I see a friend.”

lines.japanese: 私はシャベちらかすＡ君に素早く告げた（あの子は友達だけど君は友達ではありませんよ、という行間のニュアンスをぜひ読みとっていただきたい）。
lines.english: I quickly inform the babbling A. (Please, please read the implication between the lines: she's a friend, but you are not.)

lines.japanese: 「たかうちー」
lines.english: “Takauchi!”

lines.japanese: そして私は逃げだした。
lines.english: And I run away.

lines.japanese: しかし建前上ああは言ったものの、実のところ高内昌子とも“友達”というほどの仲ではない。駆けよって抱きつくなどもってのほかだ、気持ちわるい。
lines.english: But although that was my excuse, Masako Takauchi and I aren't really close enough to call each other ‘friends.’ Running over and hugging her would be out of the question. Creepy.

lines.japanese: 「……なんだよ」
lines.english: “...What?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　なにも？」
lines.english: “Huh? Nothing?”

lines.japanese: 高内は勘のするどい子だった。
lines.english: Takauchi is a perceptive girl.

lines.japanese: 「んだよ、私べつに間違ったこと言ってなくね？　あんなん、嫌いなら嫌いって言やーいいじゃん」
lines.english: “What? I'm not wrong, am I? If you don't like those guys, just say you don't like them.”

lines.japanese: とくに何か言ったわけでもないのに、彼女は通りすぎざまの一瞥だけで、先ほどの空域に生じていた不穏な気配を察したようである。
lines.english: I haven't said anything in particular, but it seems a passing glance was enough for her to sense the tension hanging over that patch of air.

lines.japanese: とはいえ、その忠告自体は誉めるに値しない。
lines.english: That doesn't mean the advice itself deserves any praise.

lines.japanese: 「はーあ。そんな簡単な問題なら、私はとっくにそうしてるよ」
lines.english: “Oh, come on. If it were that simple, I'd have done it ages ago.”

lines.japanese: 「簡単な問題だろー、グズグズにしてんのは渡来の優柔不断さだっつーの」
lines.english: “It is that simple. Your dithering is what's dragging it out, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「……あれ？　ひょっとして、私いま叱られてる？」
lines.english: “...Wait. Am I being scolded?”

lines.japanese: 「うーわ出たよ、モテる女の私は悪くない発言。ありえね、渡来マジ鬼だな。少なくともさ、惚れられるような隙見せちゃった時点で、あんたにも非はあんでしょう」
lines.english: “Oh wow, there it is. ‘I’m popular, so I can’t be at fault.’ Unbelievable. You’re a total monster, Watarai. At the very least, letting them think they had a chance makes this partly your fault.”

lines.japanese: 「大体あんた最近ちょっとチョヅき過ぎじゃね？　なんだっけえ、プリンセスとかゆっちゃってえ？　小悪魔気どりで、オトコばっさばさ泣かしちゃってえ？　で私は悪くないとか、ナンダソレどんだけ偽善者だよ」
lines.english: “Seriously, haven’t you been getting a little full of yourself lately? What was it, ‘Princess’? Playing the little tease, making guys cry left and right? Then saying it’s not your fault? What the hell? How much of a hypocrite can you be?”

lines.japanese: 「……あれ？　ひょっとして、むしろ罵られてる？」
lines.english: “...Wait. Am I actually being insulted?”

lines.japanese: 「あん？　陰でねちねち言われるよかマシじゃね？　みんな何気に渡来には甘いけどさ、三年の女子とか絶対あんたのことチョー言ってるって」
lines.english: “Huh? Better than having people bitch about you behind your back, isn't it? Everyone goes pretty easy on you, but I bet the third-year girls are saying a whole lot about you.”

lines.japanese: 「やめて。私の豊かな想像力を刺激しないで。意外と被害妄想つよいんだから」
lines.english: “Stop. Don't stimulate my rich imagination. I'm surprisingly paranoid.”

lines.japanese: 「きゃはは、ざまあじゃん渡来。超ウケるー」
lines.english: “Ahahaha! Serves you right, Watarai. That's hilarious.”

lines.japanese: まあ高内っていうのはこういう子だ。
lines.english: Well, that's the kind of girl Takauchi is.

lines.japanese: クラスの女子のリーダー的存在というか、番長的存在というか。
lines.english: Sort of the leader of the girls in our class. Or more like their gang boss.

lines.japanese: まとまらない学級会議を強引にぴしゃりと締めたりする手腕は評価するけども、個人的にはあまり率先して話しかけたいタイプではない。
lines.english: I appreciate how she can firmly shut down a class meeting that's going nowhere, but she's not someone I'd personally go out of my way to talk to.

lines.japanese: つまり、渡来明日香・海のようなココロ育成計画に立ちはだかる障害パート２。一難去ってまた一難だね。人生ってやつは試練の連続だね。
lines.english: In other words, obstacle number two in Asuka Watarai's Plan to Cultivate a Heart as Vast as the Sea. Out of the frying pan and into the fire. Life really is one trial after another.

lines.japanese: 「つか逆に聞くけどさ、オメあーゆーの、なんでハッキシ断んねーの？」
lines.english: “Okay, let me ask you this instead. Why don't you just turn guys like that down?”

lines.japanese: 「なんで。断るもなにも、私なんら決断せまられてないし」
lines.english: “Why? Turn them down for what? Nobody's asking me to make any decision.”

lines.japanese: 「告らンなくたって空気で分かんでしょ。分かった時点で言ったれって、コレ逆に優しさよ？」
lines.english: “They don't have to say it. You can tell, right? Once you can tell, let 'em have it. It's actually kinder, you know?”

lines.japanese: 「え、何も聞かれてないのに、自分から『私はあなたに恋愛感情を持つ予定はありません』とか言うの？　頭おかしいひとだよ、それ」
lines.english: “Huh? Even though they haven't asked anything, I'm supposed to announce, ‘I have no plans to develop romantic feelings for you’? I'd sound insane.”

lines.japanese: 「しょーがねえじゃん。人間って恋愛すると馬鹿ンなんだもん、正気で馬鹿の相手なんか出来るかって」
lines.english: “Can't help it. People turn into idiots when they fall in love. You can't deal with idiots by staying sane.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあ、大人。でもソレやめなー？　高内ってキホン周りをこう見てるでしょー」
lines.english: “Wow, how grown-up. But you should stop doing that. You basically look at everyone like this, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 私は指先を目から斜め下４５度へ向けた。高内は微塵も否定せず、加えて言った。
lines.english: I point my fingers from my eyes downward at a forty-five-degree angle. Takauchi doesn't deny it in the least. She just adds:

lines.japanese: 「よくゆーわ。渡来だってそうなくせに」
lines.english: “Look who's talking. You do the same thing.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　そんなことないって」
lines.english: “Huh? No, I don't.”

lines.japanese: ギクリとしないでもないけど、いやいや違う違う、それは違うよ。分かってないね番長。
lines.english: I can't say that doesn't hit a nerve, but no, no, no. That's not it. You don't get it, Boss.

lines.japanese: 私はみんなの上に立ってるわけじゃなくて、そんな大したものじゃなくて、ただみんなっていう枠からはみ出しちゃってるだけ──
lines.english: I'm not standing above everyone. I'm nothing so grand. I've just slipped outside the frame everyone else is in—

lines.japanese: ──みんなと同じ高度にはいるんだけど、むしろ緯度や経度にズレがあるんだよ。上とか下とかじゃなくて、言うなれば、なんだか私にとっては外国のひとたちを眺めてる気分なんだ。なんちゃ（略）
lines.english: —I'm at the same altitude, but my latitude and longitude are off. It's not about being above or below. If anything, watching them feels like watching people from another country. Just kid—(etc.)

lines.japanese: たとえば身近な例を挙げれば、えーと、音楽。
lines.english: For a familiar example, let's see... music.

lines.japanese: ちまたを賑わすヒットナンバー、着メロ定番のキラーチューン、クラスのみんなを夢中にさせるあの歌この歌を、どうしてか私はほとんど好きだった覚えがない。
lines.english: The hits everyone's talking about, the killer tunes everyone uses as ringtones, all the songs my classmates go crazy over—for some reason, I can hardly remember ever liking them.

lines.japanese: いわゆる大衆受け、いわゆる流行という概念に反発心があるわけじゃないから、べつに聴いたり覚えたりカラオケで歌ったり「イイよね～」なんて語りあったりはするんだけど、うーん、ごめん正直テキトーだ。
lines.english: It's not that I object to the ideas of mass appeal or trends. I listen, learn the words, sing them at karaoke, and join in with ‘It's so good, right?’ But, hmm... sorry. Honestly, I'm just going through the motions.

lines.japanese: ちなみに私のお気に入りは、最近だとアンビエントな音響系。興味があったら調べて二、三聴いてくれたまえ。
lines.english: For the record, lately I've been into ambient soundscapes. If you're interested, look it up and give a couple of tracks a listen.

lines.japanese: もし趣味が合うようだったら今度じっくり語らおう。合わなかった場合は、まあ、そうだねえ、高内さんのメアドでも教えてあげるよ。
lines.english: If our tastes match, let's have a good long talk sometime. If they don't, well, let's see... I could give you Takauchi's email address.

lines.japanese: 「てか、おまえ顔には出さないけど、ぶっちゃけ人間嫌いっぽいよね」
lines.english: “You know, you don't show it, but you kinda seem to hate people.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと」
lines.english: “What did you say?”

lines.japanese: なぜ分かった。ちくしょう。
lines.english: How did she know? Damn it.

lines.japanese: たしかに嫌いだ。でもそれはたぶん、高内が思ってる意味ともまたちょっと違うと思う。
lines.english: It's true. I do. But probably not quite in the way Takauchi means.

lines.japanese: ひとと交われば少なからず面倒は生じるし、理想は遠ざかるし、自分の感性が一般的じゃないって痛感させられる。だから私は人間と関わることが好きじゃない。
lines.english: Dealing with people inevitably brings trouble, pushes my ideals farther away, and makes me painfully aware that my sensibilities aren't ordinary. That's why I don't like getting involved with people.

lines.japanese: でもね、私は遠くからみんなを眺めてる分には、本当に微笑ましい気持ちになれるんだ。
lines.english: But when I'm just watching everyone from a distance, I really can feel warm and affectionate toward them.

lines.japanese: 素直にみんないいなあって思う。どいつもこいつも羨ましいなあって思う。世界中すべての人間を愛しいとさえ思ってしまう。まあ、私に関わってくれない限りはね。なんち（略）
lines.english: I honestly think they're wonderful. I envy every last one of them. I even feel love for every person in the world. As long as they don't get involved with me, that is. Just k—(etc.)

lines.japanese: 「んで？　さっきのふたり以外に、いまあんたにアピってくる男どんぐらいいんの？」
lines.english: “So? Apart from those two, how many guys are trying to get your attention right now?”

lines.japanese: おいおい、私の思想思索はもはや壮大な人類愛にまで及んでるというのに、高内昌子、キミはまだそんなミクロな下世話ネタを引っぱるのかね。
lines.english: Come on. My philosophical musings have already grown into a grand love for humanity, and you, Masako Takauchi, are still dwelling on such microscopic gossip?

lines.japanese: 教室までの道のり、少しの空白も見過ごさないとばかりに彼女は空虚な会話ですべて塗りつぶそうとするけれど、残念だよ番長、そんな性分がまず私と合わないんだ。
lines.english: As we walk to the classroom, she tries to paint over every last moment of silence with empty chatter. Sorry, Boss. That very disposition is one of the reasons we don't get along.

lines.japanese: たとえば何時間も黙ったまま、共に空や雲やお陽さまを眺めて過ごす（一時間に一回ぐらい「いい天気だね」「そうだね」なんて会話はあっていいかも）、そんな友人が私は欲しい。
lines.english: I'd like a friend who could spend hours in silence with me, just looking at the sky, the clouds, and the sun. (Maybe once an hour, we could say, ‘Nice weather.’ ‘It is.’)

lines.japanese: いや、分かる。分かるよ。私たちぐらいの年代の子は本当に異性や恋愛の話が好きで、たしかにそれは全人類があまねく備えている情動で、ゆえに誰しもが参加しやすいテーマではあるんだけど──
lines.english: No, I get it. I do. Kids our age really love talking about the opposite sex and romance. Those feelings are common to all humanity, so it's a subject anyone can join in on—

lines.japanese: ──実際、私もまったく興味がないわけではないし、ときには「あ、いまの彼氏？」なんて自ら振ったりもする場合もあるんだけど──
lines.english: —and I'm not completely uninterested myself. Sometimes I even start it with something like, ‘Oh, was that your boyfriend?’—

lines.japanese: ──でも私はなんていうか、それだけじゃ嫌なんだ。そんな当たり前のことしか話さないのは、なんか漠然と嫌なんだ。嫌なんだって言ってるのに、高内昌子は相も変わらずだらだらと。
lines.english: —but, I don't know. I don't want that to be all there is. Something about talking only about things so obvious just bothers me. It bothers me, I tell you, yet Masako Takauchi keeps going on and on.

lines.japanese: 「どーなん。ねえちょっと、もう手ぇ出しちゃったンとか、一人二人いんじゃねーの。隠すなって」
lines.english: “So, come on. Hey, haven't you already gotten your hands on one or two? Don't hide it.”

lines.japanese: はあ。
lines.english: Sigh.

lines.japanese: あまり気は進まないけど、私はなるべく使わないよう心がけている切り札を使った。
lines.english: I'm not very keen on it, but I play the trump card I try to use as little as possible.

lines.japanese: 「てか私、彼氏いるし」
lines.english: “Actually, I have a boyfriend.”

lines.japanese: 「うそつけ」
lines.english: “Bullshit.”

lines.japanese: 「嘘じゃないって」
lines.english: “I'm not lying.”

lines.japanese: 何を言われようが聞かれようが、自分にはもう特定の異性がいる、あとはその一点張りで徹した。
lines.english: Whatever she says or asks, I stick to that one point: there's already one particular guy in my life.

lines.japanese: ええ、はい。申しおくれたけど私には恋人がいるんですよ。
lines.english: Yes, that's right. I forgot to mention it, but I have a boyfriend.

lines.japanese: 高内もＡ君もＢ君もクラスのみんなも半信半疑、というかたぶん信じてないけども、事実として私には“彼氏”がいる。羽田鷹志という名の“恋人”。
lines.english: Takauchi, A, B, and everyone in class are half-convinced—or probably not convinced at all—but it's a fact that I have a ‘boyfriend.’ A ‘lover’ named Takashi Haneda.

lines.japanese: ね。もういいじゃないか、それで。終わろうよこの話。続きはネットで。
lines.english: See? Isn't that enough? Let's end this conversation. Take the rest online.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ羽田のどんなとこが好きなん？」
lines.english: “So what do you like about Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「どんなとこ……」
lines.english: “What do I like...”

lines.japanese: さあ？
lines.english: Who knows?

lines.japanese: そもそも彼はどんな人間なのか？
lines.english: What sort of person is he in the first place?

lines.japanese: 想像力がたくましいことは知ってる。見習いたい。あとは、何をされても笑って許せる心の広さ……とか。他は知らない。
lines.english: I know he has a powerful imagination. I'd like to learn from him. And he's bighearted enough to smile and forgive anything... I suppose. I don't know anything else.

lines.japanese: 「……考えとこ」
lines.english: “...I'll think about it.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、要するに全部好きってやつ？」
lines.english: “Oh, no, I mean, I guess I like everything?”

lines.japanese: 「かーッ、ますますウソくせ。ま、いいや、こんど羽田の方に聞くから」
lines.english: “Ha! Now it sounds even more fake. Whatever. I'll ask Haneda next time.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、ちょ、ちょ。それはいかん」
lines.english: “Wait, wait, wait. Don't do that.”

lines.japanese: 彼には世話になっている。あまり面倒をかけたくない。私はじゃれるように高内の腕をつかんだ。
lines.english: He's helping me out. I don't want to cause him too much trouble. I grab Takauchi's arm as though I'm just playing around.

lines.japanese: そのとき何か──気配のような何か、を背中に感じた気がした。
lines.english: Just then, I think I feel something at my back. Something like a presence.

lines.japanese: 振りかえる。校舎へ向かう同じ制服姿がちらほらいるだけだ。
lines.english: I look around. Just a few students in the same uniform heading toward the school building.

lines.japanese: 「どしたん」
lines.english: “What's up?”

lines.japanese: 「や、なんか後ろから殺気のような悪寒が」
lines.english: “Nothing. Just got a chill down my back. Like somebody wanted me dead.”

lines.japanese: 「きゃはは、だっせー渡来、敵つくりすぎなんだよ」
lines.english: “Ahahaha, pathetic. You've made too many enemies, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで！　知らないよ。身に覚えない」
lines.english: “Why?! I don't know what you're talking about. I haven't done anything.”

lines.japanese: 「やーっべ、神ってアイツ、ちょお公平だな。見てくれイイやつには、ちゃんとデメリット付けてんじゃん。すっげー、したら私、神めっちゃ尊敬するしね」
lines.english: “Damn, that God guy’s seriously fair. Makes sure the good-looking ones get their downsides too. Awesome. If that’s how it works, I totally respect him.”

lines.japanese: 「私なにも悪いことしてないのに……」
lines.english: “I haven't done anything wrong...”

lines.japanese: 神を呪いながら、嫌な話相手と共に校門をくぐった。
lines.english: Cursing God, I pass through the school gates with my unpleasant conversation partner.

lines.japanese: 嫌な話相手とは昇降口で別れた。
lines.english: We part at the entrance where we change our shoes.

lines.japanese: きっと、私が彼女との対話にさして面白みを見出せなかったのと同様、彼女も私に対して格別の興味を持たなかったんだろう。
lines.english: Just as I didn't find talking to her particularly interesting, she probably didn't take much interest in me either.

lines.japanese: 私がＡ君を振りきって高内を選んだように、彼女もあっさり私を捨てて通りすがりのＣ子ちゃんを追いかけていった。
lines.english: As I'd ditched A for her, she easily abandons me to chase after C, a girl passing by.

lines.japanese: めでたし、めでたし。
lines.english: And they all lived happily ever after.

lines.japanese: 高内ねえ、うーん、嫌いとまでは言わないけど。私、心の広い人間だし？
lines.english: Takauchi... hmm. I wouldn't go so far as to say I dislike her. I'm bighearted, aren't I?

lines.japanese: ただ、もう、向こう一ヵ月ぐらいは無くてもいいかな、あの子と話すのは。
lines.english: But I could probably do without another conversation with her for, oh, a month or so.

lines.japanese: そうして肩の荷と外履きを下駄箱へ置いてきた私は、ふわりふわりと舞うように廊下を渡った。
lines.english: Having left both my burden and my outdoor shoes at the shoe lockers, I float down the hallway as if I'm dancing.

lines.japanese: ここは一階エントランスロビー。美空学園の玄関口だ。
lines.english: This is the first-floor entrance lobby. The front door of Misora Academy.

lines.japanese: 玄関はその家のカオとか言うよね。うん、じゃあ、これがうちの学校のカオだ。見栄っぱりの成金趣味。
lines.english: They say a house's entrance is its face. Right. So this is our school's face. Showy, nouveau-riche taste.

lines.japanese: どうだワシの学校すごいじゃろう、っていうね。創設者の想いがね。伝わってくるよね、悪い意味で。
lines.english: ‘Well, now! Isn’t my school magnificent?’ The founder’s feelings come through loud and clear. In a bad way.

lines.japanese: そもそも何故この柳木原という街に学び舎を建てたのかね創設者どの。周り中フツーにビルだらけですよ。
lines.english: Why did you build a school in Yanagihara of all places, dear founder? Buildings everywhere you look.

lines.japanese: 「どうなんだねキミ」
lines.english: “What do you think, my dear?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Pardon?”

lines.japanese: 無愛想な表情でずんずん近付いてきた後輩にとつぜん矛先を向けてみたが、相手は顔色ひとつ変えなかった。
lines.english: I suddenly turn my attack on a younger student striding toward me with an unfriendly expression, but her face doesn't change at all.

lines.japanese: 「あの先輩。すみませんが、質問の意図が分かりかねます」
lines.english: “Excuse me, Miss Watarai, but I'm afraid I don't understand the purpose of your question.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、意図なんて、ないもんそんなの。意図のない質問で、玉泉を困惑させようという意図だけだもん」
lines.english: “Well, there isn't one. Unless you count my intention to confuse you with a question that has no intention behind it.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、それはご期待に添えず失礼いたしました」
lines.english: “I see. My apologies for failing to meet your expectations.”

lines.japanese: 玉泉の反応はあまりに慇懃で、かえってふざけてるみたいにも見える。何事も行きすぎると冗談じみてしまう見本みたいな子──この美人な真面目ちゃんが１年Ｂ組・玉泉日和子だ。
lines.english: Tamaizumi's response is so excessively polite it almost looks like she's joking. A living example of how anything taken too far begins to seem like a joke. This pretty, earnest girl is Hiyoko Tamaizumi of class 1-B.

lines.japanese: 学年違いで共に帰宅部という私と彼女の接点は、月に一度の美化委員会。全校各クラスの代表委員が集まるその定例会議、今月はきのう行われたばかり。のはず。たしか。いま思いだしたんだけども。
lines.english: We're in different grades, and neither of us belongs to a club. Our point of contact is the monthly school beautification committee meeting, where representatives of every class gather. This month's meeting was yesterday. Supposedly. If I remember right. Which I've only just done.

lines.japanese: 「あー、それでか……」
lines.english: “Oh, so that's why...”

lines.japanese: というわけで私は、ただでさえ日ごろから笑い分の不足している玉泉日和子が、今朝はことさらに鉄仮面みたいな顔をしている、その理由に思いあたってしまった。
lines.english: And so I realize why Hiyoko Tamaizumi, who never has much of a smile to spare anyway, looks particularly like she's wearing an iron mask this morning.

lines.japanese: 「おはようございます」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 彼女はスクールバッグの手提げを両手で持ったまま、小さく頭を下げた。
lines.english: Holding her schoolbag's handles in both hands, she dips her head slightly.

lines.japanese: 「はよう」
lines.english: “Morning.”

lines.japanese: 私は同じかばんを片手で肩に担ぎ歩きだす。すたすた歩きだす。当たり前のように玉泉も付いてきた。すたすた付いてきた。
lines.english: I sling an identical bag over one shoulder and start walking. Briskly. Naturally, Tamaizumi follows. Briskly.

lines.japanese: 「渡来先輩」
lines.english: “Miss Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 待てやコラと同じトーンで私を呼ぶ後輩。私は歩きつづける。すたすた歩きつづける。玉泉もぴったり付いてきた。すたすた付いてきた。
lines.english: The younger student calls my name in the same tone as ‘Hold it right there, you.’ I keep walking. Briskly. Tamaizumi stays right on my heels. Briskly.

lines.japanese: 「きのうの委員会、どうしていらっしゃらなかったんですか」
lines.english: “May I ask why you were absent from yesterday’s committee meeting?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あれねえ、ごめんねえ。あのー、ちょっと、風邪？　そう風邪が、うん、ごはっごほっ」
lines.english: “Oh, that. Sorry. Um, I had a bit of a... cold? Yes, a cold. Mm-hm. Cough, cough.”

lines.japanese: 「体育の授業では、ぴんぴんしていたという証言があるんですけど」
lines.english: “There are witnesses who say you were perfectly lively in gym class.”

lines.japanese: 「なに。誰だ、誰がちくった」
lines.english: “What? Who? Who squealed?”

lines.japanese: あとでシメてやる。
lines.english: I'll get them later.

lines.japanese: しかし玉泉は、私の追及を無視して顎をそびやかした。
lines.english: But Tamaizumi ignores my interrogation and lifts her chin.

lines.japanese: 「渡来先輩、ふざけてるんですか？」
lines.english: “Miss Watarai, are you making fun of me?”

lines.japanese: 「玉泉後輩、君は度胸があるねえ。上級生に対しての、躊躇や遠慮というものが見られない」
lines.english: “You've got some nerve, Tamaizumi. Not a hint of hesitation or deference toward an upperclassman.”

lines.japanese: これはおふざけじゃなく。事実、私は彼女の肝の太さに感心していた。同時に憂えてもいたけれど。
lines.english: I'm not joking about that. I'm genuinely impressed by her nerve, although I'm worried at the same time.

lines.japanese: この子、こんな調子で長生きできるのかしら。私は海のような広い心の上級生だから、この程度のこと笑って済ませられるけども。
lines.english: Will she live long, acting like this? I'm an upperclassman with a heart as vast as the sea, so I can laugh this much off.

lines.japanese: 「私、間違ったこと言ってませんから」
lines.english: “I'm not saying anything wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「青い」
lines.english: “Naive.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「青いよ玉泉。正論なら声を大にしてもいいなんて信じてるなら、もう少し世間の荒波に揉まれた方がいいね。そう。そう思う親心から、私はいま心を鬼にして君をおちょくっているんだぜ？」
lines.english: “You're naive, Tamaizumi. If you think being right means you can say it as loudly as you like, you need a little more battering from the rough seas of life. Yes. It's out of that parental concern that I'm hardening my heart and teasing you now, you know?”

lines.japanese: 「頼んでません。結構です」
lines.english: “I didn't ask you to. No, thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「ねーねー、上級生の好意を断るときはさ、嘘でも愛想笑いとか添えといた方がよくない？」
lines.english: “Hey, hey. When you’re turning down an upperclassman’s kindness, shouldn’t you at least throw in a friendly smile? Even a fake one?”

lines.japanese: 「無理です。それでは相手に対して、怒りのニュアンスが伝わりません」
lines.english: “I can't. That wouldn't convey my anger to the other person.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なに、玉泉いま怒ってんの？」
lines.english: “Huh? What, you're angry right now?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、わりと」
lines.english: “Yes. Quite.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese: 「渡来先輩が休むと私の仕事が増えます。各特別教室の清掃用具チェックと整頓、欠品の補充手続き、その他もろもろの雑務……」
lines.english: “When you're absent, I have more work to do. Checking and organizing the cleaning supplies in the special-purpose classrooms, arranging replacements for anything missing, and various other chores...”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうなんだ。あらあら。いいよ、じゃあソレ、私やるから」
lines.english: “Oh, is that so? My, my. Okay, I'll do those, then.”

lines.japanese: 「もうやっちゃいました」
lines.english: “I've already done them.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？　やるなよ」
lines.english: “Why? Don't do them.”

lines.japanese: 「やりたくてやったわけじゃありません！」
lines.english: “It's not as though I wanted to!”

lines.japanese: 「おっとォ」
lines.english: “Whoa there.”

lines.japanese: 私は手を×字に交差させて、荒ぶる玉泉を押しとどめた。
lines.english: I cross my hands in an X to hold back the raging Tamaizumi.

lines.japanese: 彼女は咳払いするような仕草とともに言葉を続けた。
lines.english: She makes a small throat-clearing motion and continues.

lines.japanese: 「仕方なかったんですよ。私がやらなかったら、渡来先輩がさぼったこと、三年のひとたちにばれそうだったし……」
lines.english: “I didn't have a choice. If I hadn't done them, the third-years would probably have found out you skipped the meeting...”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あ、それで？　なの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, so... that's why?”

lines.japanese: つまり？　私をかばうために自ら面倒をかぶってくれたと？
lines.english: Meaning? She took the trouble on herself to cover for me?

lines.japanese: ええ？　あらあら、まじですか？　すっごくいい子じゃないですか玉泉日和子。先輩カンゲキ。
lines.english: Really? My, my, are you serious? Isn't Hiyoko Tamaizumi a wonderful girl? One happy upperclassman!

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 私は並んで歩いていた後輩の正面に立ちふさがって、がっちり両肩を掴んだ。
lines.english: I step in front of the younger girl walking beside me and take a firm hold of both her shoulders.
“Huh? Huh?”

lines.japanese: 瞬間、うろたえる玉泉。
lines.english: Tamaizumi immediately loses her composure.

lines.japanese: 私は彼女の弱点を知っている。彼女の苦手な間合いを知っている。
lines.english: I know her weakness. I know the distance she can't handle.

lines.japanese: 「な、なんですかいきなり……」
lines.english: “Wh-what is this, all of a sudden...?”

lines.japanese: 玉泉日和子は、相手の目を見て話せない子なのだ。
lines.english: Hiyoko Tamaizumi can't look people in the eye when she talks to them.

lines.japanese: 自らに正義さえあれば、先輩にも男子にも教員にも、物怖じせず真っ向から対峙する。
lines.english: As long as she's in the right, she'll face down upperclassmen, boys, even teachers without flinching.

lines.japanese: しかし注意深く観察すれば、実は瞳の焦点が相手の目ではなく微妙にその下、鼻や口や襟元を捕えていると気付く。
lines.english: But watch carefully, and you'll notice that her eyes aren't actually focused on theirs. She looks just below them, at their nose, mouth, or collar.

lines.japanese: 加えて、会議中など板書する際には眼鏡を着用するぐらいだから、近視だか乱視だかの気もあるんだろう。
lines.english: What's more, she wears glasses when she writes on the board during meetings, so she's probably a little nearsighted or astigmatic, too.

lines.japanese: これらのデータが導きだす答えはひとつ。
lines.english: These facts point to one answer.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんね」
lines.english: “I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 私は裸眼の玉泉にもくっきり見える距離まで接近した。
lines.english: I move close enough for Tamaizumi to see me clearly even without her glasses.

lines.japanese: 「私のために嫌な思いさせちゃって本当ごめん。次から気を付ける。ありがとう」
lines.english: “I'm really sorry I put you through that for my sake. I'll be more careful next time. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「べ、べつに……その、いいんですけど、分かっていただければ……」
lines.english: “I-it's... um, it's all right. As long as you understand...”

lines.japanese: ぐいっ。
lines.english: Yank.

lines.japanese: あさっての方向へ曲がりかけた首をむりやり正面に戻した。
lines.english: I force her head back to face me as it starts turning off in an entirely different direction.

lines.japanese: 「ほんと？　許してくれるの？」
lines.english: “Really? You forgive me?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ……つい忘れちゃうことぐらい、誰にでもありますし……」
lines.english: “Well... Anyone can forget something now and then...”

lines.japanese: 「優しいなあ。私、玉泉がトモダチでよかった。もし今度また委員会うっかり忘れちゃったら、そのときもよろしくね？」
lines.english: “You're so kind. I'm glad you're my friend, Tamaizumi. If I happen to forget the committee meeting again, I'm counting on you then, too, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ……まあ、べつに……そのぐらい、いいですけど」
lines.english: “Well... yes, I suppose... I don't mind doing that much.”

lines.japanese: いいのかよ。
lines.english: You don't?

lines.japanese: あーあ、なんか、強いんだか弱いんだかよく分かんない子だ。
lines.english: Honestly, I can't tell whether this girl is strong or weak.

lines.japanese: 「えーっとー？　来月は何日だっけ、委員会」
lines.english: “Let's see... What day is next month's meeting?”

lines.japanese: 私はさっさと玉泉から離れて、携帯電話のスケジュール画面を呼びだした。
lines.english: I promptly step away from Tamaizumi and bring up the calendar on my cell phone.

lines.japanese: かわいい後輩のためにも、次は忘れず出席しようと思った。
lines.english: For that sweet younger girl's sake, I'll make sure I remember to attend next time.

lines.japanese: 「てかさー、私のアドレス教えとくから、悪いけど当日になったらメールくれない？　今日サボんなよ的なやつ」
lines.english: “Actually, I'll give you my email address. Sorry to ask, but could you send me a message on the day? Something like ‘Don't skip today.’”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい、いいですけど……いいんですか？」
lines.english: “Oh, yes, I can... Are you sure?”

lines.japanese: 「なにが？」
lines.english: “About what?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、丁度きのう小耳に挟んだことがあって。渡来先輩はぜったい自分からメアド教えてくれないって」
lines.english: “Well, I happened to hear something just yesterday. That you never offer anyone your email address.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、男子にはね。ちょっとジカジョー？　あはは、昔いろいろ痛い目みちゃって」
lines.english: “Oh, I don’t go handing it out to boys. Full of myself, huh? Ha ha. I’ve had some bad experiences.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえ、女子の先輩が言ってたんです」
lines.english: “Oh, no. It was one of the older girls who said it.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　女子には教えるよ、そんなフツーに……」
lines.english: “Huh? I give it to girls. Of course...”

lines.japanese: 普通に……いや、あんまり教えないか。
lines.english: Of course... No, I don't give it out much, do I?

lines.japanese: あれ？　あれあれ？　ひょっとして私、いつになく社交的？
lines.english: Huh? Huh, huh? Am I being unusually sociable?

lines.japanese: ふむ。玉泉日和子か。この子とは意外と相性合うのかもしれない。
lines.english: Hmm. Hiyoko Tamaizumi. Maybe we get along better than I'd expected.

lines.japanese: 「玉泉、アンビエントとか聴く？」
lines.english: “Tamaizumi, do you listen to ambient music?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　なんですかいきなり」
lines.english: “What? Why are you asking that all of a sudden?”

lines.japanese: やっぱり違うか。
lines.english: Or maybe not.

lines.japanese: 「嫌いではないですけど」
lines.english: “I don't dislike it, though.”

lines.japanese: 「友達になろう」
lines.english: “Let's be friends.”

lines.japanese: 本当の意味で。
lines.english: In the real sense.

lines.japanese: 「あと、昭和の歌謡曲とか」
lines.english: “And older Japanese pop songs—from the Showa era, that sort of thing.”

lines.japanese: 「それは……う、ううん、じゃあ今度聴いてみる」
lines.english: “That's... N-no, okay. I'll give them a listen sometime.”

lines.japanese: 趣味の広い人間になろうと思った。
lines.english: I decide to be someone with broader tastes.

lines.japanese: 朝の教室は全国チェーンの喫茶店みたいに程よくざわついていた。
lines.english: The morning classroom has a comfortable hum of conversation, like a national-chain coffee shop.

lines.japanese: そこここに点在するいくつかのグループへ、挨拶を投げたり投げかえしたりしながら自分の席へ向かう。
lines.english: I make my way to my seat, exchanging greetings with the little groups scattered around the room.

lines.japanese: 途中“彼氏”と目が合った。
lines.english: On the way, I meet my ‘boyfriend's’ eyes.

lines.japanese: 私は「ん？」と窺うように口角を上げる。自分で言うのもアレだが、なかなかいい笑顔だと思う。内緒だが鏡の前で練習したこともある。
lines.english: I lift the corners of my mouth in an inquiring little ‘Hm?’ I shouldn't say so myself, but I think it's a pretty good smile. Between you and me, I've practiced it in the mirror.

lines.japanese: しかし彼は、まるで溜息でもつくように唇をねじ曲げただけで、すぐに俯いて表情を隠す。いつも通りのつれない反応だ。
lines.english: But he only twists his lips as if he's sighing, then immediately looks down to hide his expression. His usual chilly response.

lines.japanese: 仮にも“恋人”同士なんだからもうちょっと親睦を深めたいとは思うのだけど、羽田君はつねにひとりで、クラスの誰とも距離を置いていた。
lines.english: Since we're supposedly ‘lovers,’ I'd like us to get to know each other a little better, but Haneda is always alone, keeping his distance from everyone in class.

lines.japanese: ときおり一部の男子や女子から意地の悪い交流を持ちかけられることもあったけど、そんなとき彼は決して怒らず、決して嘆かず、ただそっと物憂げに微笑う。
lines.english: Sometimes a few of the boys or girls go out of their way to be nasty to him, but he never gets angry, never complains. He just smiles quietly and wistfully.

lines.japanese: 立ちいったことは聞けないけれど、きっと羽田君には何かがあるんだろう。孤独を選び、周囲に絶望するだけの背景が、その過去には秘められているに違いない。
lines.english: I can't ask anything too personal, but there must be something going on with Haneda. Surely his past hides something that would make him choose solitude and despair of the people around him.

lines.japanese: だけど彼は入学以来、私の持ちかけたしょーもない恋人設定の芝居に、いまだ付きあってくれている。とてもいいひとだ。本人は気にするなと言ってくれるけど、やっぱり申しわけないと思う。
lines.english: But ever since we started at this school, he's kept playing along with the silly pretend-romance I proposed. He's a very good person. He tells me not to worry, but I still feel bad.

lines.japanese: だから、せいぜい私は彼女ぶって付きまとったりせず、なにか申し出がないかぎりは干渉しないようにしたい。それが、ひとりきりの時間を好む彼への、せめてもの礼だ。
lines.english: So at the very least, I don't want to cling to him, acting like his girlfriend. Unless he asks for something, I'll try not to interfere. It's the least I can do to thank someone who likes having time to himself.

lines.japanese: でも、たまにはちょっと、実のない雑談でもいいから、うん、話とかしてみたいと思うんだ。趣味とか思考とか、たぶん合いそうな気がするんだ。どこか深いところで、私と同じにおいを感じるんだよ。
lines.english: But sometimes I'd like to talk a little, even if it's just empty chatter. I have a feeling our tastes and ways of thinking might match. Somewhere deep down, I sense something in him that feels like me.

lines.japanese: いや待て、いかんいかん。ただでさえ私は、変な芝居を押しつけちゃってるイタタな迷惑女なんだ。これ以上うざがられるような、そんな、恩を仇で返すようなことはしちゃいかん。自重しよう。
lines.english: No, wait. No, no. I'm already an embarrassing nuisance, saddling him with this weird act. I can't repay his kindness by making myself even more annoying. Restrain yourself.

lines.japanese: いろいろ話しかけたい衝動を抑え、私は何食わぬ顔で羽田君の横を通りすぎる。
lines.english: Suppressing the urge to say all sorts of things, I pass beside Haneda as if nothing is happening.

lines.japanese: もしかしたら今日あたり、何かの気まぐれで「あ、渡来さん？」なんて呼びかけてくれることを期待してみたけども、やっぱりそんなことはなかった。
lines.english: I let myself hope that maybe today, on a whim, he might call, ‘Oh, Watarai?’ But of course he doesn't.

lines.japanese: 彼の机の横で、何気なく速度を落とした自分が馬鹿みたいだ。
lines.english: I feel stupid for casually slowing down beside his desk.

lines.japanese: 明日は目の前ですっ転んでみるかね。
lines.english: Maybe tomorrow I'll try falling flat on my face in front of him.
